expectation: A membrane ring at cell-cell junctions on epithelial (tumour) cells. It should be common in carcinoma and sit in cohesive nests, glands and sheets, with Ecad-negative stroma and immune areas between them. Invasive cells may show less.
observed: A: sharp yellow tumour nests, glands and villous epithelium, with dark stroma between them. Some cores have little epithelium and stay dark. B and C: honeycomb membrane outlines on epithelial clusters and glands, and the stroma is negative. D: a polygonal junctional network.
why: Ecad gives crisp membrane honeycombs restricted to epithelial nests and glands, and the stroma is negative, as a real E-cadherin stain should look.
notes: Ecad outlines epithelial cell membranes in tumour nests and glands across most cores, with a clear junctional honeycomb and dark stroma between. Cores with little epithelium stay dark.
